title: Pavonia
description: Michiel Pauw, a director of the West India Company, buys the west bank of the North River from the Lenape - Hoboken, then Ahasimus and Aressick - for the patroonship he calls Pavonia. The first houses rise at Communipaw and Harsimus within a few years.

title: Hempstead
description: English families from Stamford, Connecticut, settle on the great plains of Long Island under a patent from Director Kieft; their town will hold the south half of today's Nassau County.

title: Oyster Bay
description: Peter Wright, Samuel Mayo and William Leverich buy land from the Matinecock sachem Assiapum and found Oyster Bay, on the harbour that the Hartford treaty of 1650 made the border between New Netherland and New England.

title: Bergen
description: Stuyvesant orders a palisaded village laid out on the ridge behind Communipaw. Bergen, with its square and four gates, is the first permanent town in New Jersey and gets its own court the next year.

title: The Elizabethtown Purchase
description: Weeks after the English take New Netherland, men from Long Island buy the land between the Raritan and the Passaic from the Lenape. Elizabethtown becomes the first English town and the first capital of New Jersey.

title: Newark
description: Puritans from Milford, Branford and New Haven, led by Robert Treat, land on the Passaic and lay out a town along a broad street with a training place and a market place.

title: East Jersey's Four Counties
description: The assembly of East Jersey divides the province into Bergen, Essex, Middlesex and Monmouth counties. Bergen and Essex later give up Passaic (1837), Hudson (1840) and Union (1857).

title: The Tappan Patent
description: Governor Dongan grants the valley of the Sparkill to sixteen Dutch families from Manhattan; Tappan becomes the seat of Orange County.

title: New Rochelle
description: Huguenot refugees settle on 6,000 acres that Jacob Leisler buys for them from John Pell, lord of Pelham Manor.

title: Philipsburg Manor
description: A royal charter makes Frederick Philipse lord of a manor that runs from Spuyten Duyvil to the Croton River, with tenant farms and mills at Yonkers and on the Pocantico.

title: The Society for Useful Manufactures
description: Alexander Hamilton's Society for Establishing Useful Manufactures is chartered by New Jersey and chooses the Great Falls of the Passaic for a planned industrial city, Paterson. Its raceways drive cotton, locomotive and silk mills for 150 years.

title: Rockland County
description: The part of Orange County south of the Highlands becomes Rockland County, with its court house at New City.

title: The Town of Jersey
description: The Associates of the Jersey Company buy Paulus Hook and lay out a town opposite Manhattan, the beginning of Jersey City. The same year John Stevens sells the first lots of Hoboken.

title: Stevens's Steam Ferry
description: John Stevens puts the Juliana on the run between Hoboken and Manhattan, the first steam ferry in regular service anywhere.

title: The Morris Canal
description: The canal from the Delaware reaches tidewater at Newark, lifting Lehigh coal over 23 inclined planes; it is carried across Bergen Neck to Jersey City in 1836.

title: The Paterson and Hudson River Railroad
description: Horse-drawn cars begin running between Paterson and Acquackanonk; within a few years the line crosses the meadows to Jersey City behind steam locomotives.

title: The Long Island Rail Road at Hicksville
description: The railroad from Brooklyn, meant as a short cut to Boston, stops for four years at Valentine Hicks's new village on the Hempstead Plains before pushing on to Greenport in 1844.

title: Hudson County
description: The southern end of Bergen County - Jersey City and the townships of Bergen and Harrison - becomes Hudson County, the smallest county of New Jersey and soon the most crowded.

title: The Erie's Pier at Piermont
description: The New York and Erie Railroad, kept inside New York State by its charter, opens its first section, to Goshen, from the mile-long pier it built in the Tappan Zee in 1839, where passengers change to steamboats for the city.

title: Base Ball at the Elysian Fields
description: The Knickerbocker Base Ball Club plays the New York Nine on the Stevens family's pleasure grounds at Hoboken, the first recorded match under the Knickerbocker rules. The fields are built over by the 1890s.

title: The Hudson River Railroad
description: Trains run from Manhattan up the east bank to Peekskill on a causeway that cuts off the river coves from Yonkers to Croton; the line reaches the Albany shore in 1851.

title: Llewellyn Park
description: Llewellyn Haskell and the architect Alexander Jackson Davis lay out a gated residential park on the slope of Orange Mountain, the first planned garden suburb in the country.

title: Garden City
description: The merchant Alexander T. Stewart buys 7,000 acres of the Hempstead Plains from the town and builds a planned town with its own railroad.

title: Jersey City Takes the Ridge
description: Voters join Hudson City and the City of Bergen to Jersey City; Greenville follows in 1873. The Dutch town of 1660 becomes a neighbourhood.

title: The Communipaw Terminal
description: The Central Railroad of New Jersey opens its terminal on land made in Communipaw Cove. With the Erie, Pennsylvania, Lackawanna and West Shore terminals it lines the Hudson County shore with ferry houses and rail yards.

title: The First County Park
description: Essex County creates the first county park commission in the United States and takes over Newark's reservoir tract as Branch Brook Park; South Mountain and Eagle Rock reservations follow.

title: Nassau County
description: The three towns of Queens County left outside Greater New York - Hempstead, North Hempstead and Oyster Bay - become Nassau County, with its seat at Mineola.

title: Saving the Palisades
description: New York and New Jersey create the Palisades Interstate Park Commission, which buys out the quarries that are blasting the cliffs.

title: New Croton Dam
description: The tallest dam in the world when it is finished drowns the Croton Dam of 1842 and stretches the city's reservoir far up the valley.

title: Harriman's Gift
description: Mary Averell Harriman gives 10,000 acres and a million dollars for a park in the Highlands on condition that the state give up the prison it is building at Bear Mountain.

title: Port Newark
description: Newark opens a ship channel and docks dredged out of the meadows on Newark Bay; the Port Authority takes them over in 1948.

title: Black Tom
description: German agents blow up the munitions depot on Black Tom Island at the Lehigh Valley Railroad's piers. The blast breaks windows across Manhattan and scars the Statue of Liberty.

title: Bear Mountain Bridge
description: The first road bridge across the Hudson south of Albany, briefly the longest suspension span in the world, opens at the gate of the Highlands.

title: Bronx River Parkway
description: A landscaped motor road in a cleaned-up river valley opens from the Bronx to Kensico Dam, the first parkway of its kind. Westchester builds the Saw Mill, Hutchinson and Cross County parkways on its model.

title: Lindbergh Takes Off
description: Charles Lindbergh lifts the Spirit of St. Louis off the muddy runway of Roosevelt Field on the Hempstead Plains and lands in Paris 33 and a half hours later.

title: Hutchinson River Parkway
description: The parkway is open from Pelham Manor to White Plains. Like the Saw Mill River Parkway begun in the same years, it follows a stream valley bought up as park land.

title: Newark Airport
description: Newark opens an airfield on filled meadow beside its port; through the 1930s it is the busiest commercial airport in the world.

title: Jones Beach
description: Robert Moses opens a state park on a barrier beach raised with sand pumped from the bay, reached by the Wantagh causeway and, from the city, by the Southern State Parkway.

title: Bayonne Bridge
description: The longest steel arch in the world joins Bergen Point to Staten Island across the Kill Van Kull.

title: Pulaski Skyway
description: A viaduct five and a half kilometres long carries the highway from the Holland Tunnel over the Hackensack and Passaic rivers and the meadows between Jersey City and Newark.

title: Lincoln Tunnel
description: The first tube opens between Weehawken and Midtown, its looping approach cut into the Palisades. A second tube follows in 1945 and a third in 1957.

title: Levittown
description: The first families move into Levitt and Sons' houses on the potato fields of Island Trees. By 1951 there are 17,447 of them, the model of the post-war suburb.

title: New Jersey Turnpike
description: The toll road opens section by section from the Delaware; its northern end across the Newark and Hackensack meadows is finished in January 1952.

title: Garden State Parkway
description: The first toll section opens in Union County; by 1957 the parkway runs from Cape May to the New York line through Union, Essex, Passaic and Bergen counties.

title: Tappan Zee Bridge
description: The New York Thruway crosses the Hudson at its widest point, between Nyack and Tarrytown, and opens Rockland County to the suburbs.

title: The First Container Ship
description: Malcom McLean's converted tanker Ideal X sails from Port Newark with 58 trailer boxes on deck. The Port Authority builds the Elizabeth terminal next door for his Sea-Land line, and within two decades the piers of Manhattan and Brooklyn stand empty.

title: Palisades Interstate Parkway
description: The parkway along the top of the cliffs is finished from the George Washington Bridge to Bear Mountain, on land John D. Rockefeller Jr. bought up and gave in 1933.

title: The Meadowlands
description: Giants Stadium opens beside the new racetrack on filled marsh at East Rutherford, the centrepiece of the state's plan for the Hackensack Meadowlands; the arena follows in 1981.

title: A New Tappan Zee Bridge
description: The first span of the Governor Mario M. Cuomo Bridge opens beside the bridge of 1955, which is taken down by 2019.
